instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Start the Hard Part
cards.instruction: Get someone else to explain, announce, or begin the emotionally difficult part.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You tell the choir the tour's cancelled. All those projection exercises I put you through can finally do some good.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're the organiser.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And you're no longer the person who whispered through every rehearsal. I'll handle the refund forms. Give them a clear opening sentence.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They'll ask why.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Start with 'funding'. Don't soften it into 'a little problem' like you used to. I'll step in once you've got through their first reaction.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Phone Mum about selling the house. You remember how we practised difficult calls? Say what it's about before asking how she is.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She asked to speak to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you've checked who she wants. I'll take over once you've said 'selling'. You used to do that opening quite nicely.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll put her on speaker. You'll be there for the whole thing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fine. Keep your voice steady when she says my full name. Let her finish it, then hand over. Don't rush that bit this time.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: What Aren’t You Saying?
cards.instruction: Find out what someone is holding back by treating every careful answer as incomplete.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: 'Interesting' isn't a critique. I used to make you cross that word out. What did you really think of my audition?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're my sister. I'm trying to be encouraging.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You were always good at the encouraging paragraph. Now give me the one you haven't written.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your singing was better than your dancing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Better by how much? We practised being specific. Do I need a few lessons, or should I ask them for a part where I sit down?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: These minutes say 'discussion of my proposal'. I trained you to record the decision, not just that mouths opened. What happened?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sign them and we can eat. Nobody wanted an awkward record.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've learned discretion. Now remember the part about names. Who wanted mine left out?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I did. I suggested someone else present, to save your proposal.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Better. You've supplied the person making the suggestion. Now finish the sentence: who replaces me?

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Hope with Me
cards.instruction: Recruit someone into believing that the outcome can still change, even when the evidence is thin.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Draw another parade route with me. Two streets said no. You used to give up at the first line I crossed out.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The only route left goes behind the supermarket.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you've found a line we can keep. Put in the loading bay. Who might stand there and cheer?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My dad would come. He works there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Draw him in, big enough for us to see. You always left the people till last. Leave room beside him—who might he bring?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Help me choose glasses for our café. All those mornings I had you watching the customers instead of the till—show me what you learned.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're on the waiting list. I haven't even told my mum.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No announcement, then. Just show me what you'd set down in front of her if we got the place.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: A mug. She'd complain about these little glasses.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: There, you've remembered to think about the customer. Pick her a proper big one. Can you picture us putting it on her table?

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Say the Scary Part
cards.instruction: Get someone else to name the frightening possibility or vulnerable feeling before you do.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we open the landlord's letter, finish the question I used to set you: miss the rent, and then what?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We've only missed one payment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Accurate arithmetic. You always stopped there. Tell me what could happen to the shop.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We could lose it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And after Dad trusted me with it, what would that make me? Don't trail off before the hard word. I need you to finish this answer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before our qualifier, do the debrief I used to make you do. What's the result neither of us wants to say?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't want you carrying that onto the ice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I already am. You used to hide behind that answer too. Say the result first; I'll follow you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We might not qualify. I'd still want to skate with you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Now finish the other answer: what are you promising not to do if we lose? I need you to say that too.

cards.title: See What This Took
cards.instruction: Make someone recognize the courage, restraint, or emotional labor your choices required.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Here's the apology I sent, and here's the angry draft in its folder. Remember how I made you keep your rough work?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I appreciate the apology. Why show me the angry version?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Because 'sorry' took ten minutes. Deciding not to send that folder took all night. You're still only marking the finished page.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Now I'm tempted to read what you spared me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave it shut. Feel how thick it is. You used to complain when I made you cut one sentence; I need you to notice how many I didn't send.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I told the committee I won't chair another year. Remember my rule about saying no without excuses? I finally followed it myself.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Good. Could you stay until we find someone?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Listen to the whole answer. I spent an hour in your car getting those two sentences out.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then I'll tell them you're exhausted and need a break.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No extra paragraph. That's what I worked so hard to leave out. Could you tell them I said no, and tell me you know what that took?
